status: experimental interoperability architecture; no federation authority claim
purpose: Compose many bilateral recognition relationships without converting graph reachability into trust, authority, membership, eligibility, or universal equivalence.

graph_semantics.path: discoverable evidence about possible recognition relationships only
graph_semantics.local_rule: Only an explicitly adopted local edge or locally approved recognition-set entry may satisfy recognition policy.

invariants: graph path existence is not trust
shortest path is not strongest path
multiple agreeing paths are corroborative evidence only
local institutions choose which external edges or recognition sets they adopt
recognition-set membership does not grant runtime authority, membership, office, or eligibility
revocation or withdrawal of one edge does not rewrite unrelated bilateral relationships
conflicting recognition paths remain visible and locally resolved
assurance degrades to the weakest required accepted edge unless local policy demands stronger evidence
privacy restrictions compose by intersection, not union
purpose scopes compose by intersection, not union

recognition_set.meaning: A reusable list of bilateral profiles that a local institution may review and adopt as a convenience.
recognition_set.adoption_rule: Importing or discovering a recognition set never activates its members.

nonclaims: This profile does not create a supranational authority, federation government, accreditation authority, or universal trust fabric.
A federation graph is not a reputation score.
Path discovery may aid routing and interoperability planning without satisfying a proof requirement.
